item.title: Assistant Legislative Fiscal Analyst
item.description:
Application deadline: October 16, 2026 at 11:59 PM. Submit a letter of interest, résumé, and college transcript as one combined PDF to sfacjobs@sfac.virginia.gov. Selected applicants may be asked to provide three professional references and complete a writing exercise and Microsoft Excel assessment.

The Virginia Senate Finance & Appropriations Committee (SFAC) seeks an Assistant Legislative Fiscal Analyst to research and analyze legislation, state agency operations, and public policy initiatives. The analyst manages assigned policy and agency portfolios, examines complex financial and operational information, and translates findings into clear, objective analyses and recommendations for legislative and public audiences. The position offers a distinctive opportunity to contribute to consequential decisions impacting citizens throughout the Commonwealth while developing a career in nonpartisan legislative service. On-site in Richmond, VA. 2 years of relevant experience required. Salary $70,000–$80,000.

Key responsibilities include: analyzing legislation and estimating fiscal and operational impacts; researching assigned policy areas, state agency operations, and budget proposals; supporting Senate Finance & Appropriations Subcommittees in evaluating legislation and developing budget recommendations; monitoring assigned agencies and evaluating budget requests, strategic initiatives, and operational performance; developing fiscal forecasts and recommendations using financial, economic, demographic, and statistical data; preparing data visualizations, reports, issue briefs, and presentations that translate complex findings for legislative audiences; and contributing to special studies and related Committee assignments.

Qualifications: a bachelor's degree in public policy, public administration, economics, finance, accounting, business administration, political science, statistics, mathematics, data analytics, or a related analytical field (or equivalent combination of relevant education and experience); at least two years of progressively responsible professional experience in budget, financial, or policy analysis; government administration; legislative research; program evaluation; economics; public finance; strategic planning; or data analytics; advanced proficiency with Microsoft Excel including data analysis and visualization; and demonstrated ability to research, analyze, and synthesize complex fiscal, legislative, policy, and statistical information and communicate findings clearly. Master's degree preferred; government budgeting, finance, or public policy analysis experience preferred.

Compensation and logistics: salary $70,000–$80,000 commensurate with relevant education and experience. Commonwealth of Virginia benefits. On-site in Richmond, VA (professional business attire; limited telework outside legislative session). Extended hours required during legislative sessions and peak workload periods. Deadline: October 16, 2026 at 11:59 PM. Apply via combined PDF to sfacjobs@sfac.virginia.gov.

item.company: CDC – Public Health Informatics Fellowship Program
item.title: Public Health Informatics Fellow (Class of 2027)
item.description:
Application deadline: November 6, 2026. Application period opened September 1, 2026. Apply via the CDC PHIFP application portal.

Note: This is a 2-year paid fellowship, not a federal government employment position. Fellows are placed in assignments at CDC centers, institutes, and offices (CIOs) across CDC. Stipend amount not stated — confirm via the CDC PHIFP website.

The CDC Public Health Informatics Fellowship Program (PHIFP) trains professionals in the systematic application of knowledge about systems that capture, manage, analyze, and use information to improve population-level health outcomes. The Class of 2027 fellowship provides on-the-job training for professionals to apply expertise in computer science, data analytics, and data science to public health. Fellows are assigned to host sites within CDC where they work on advanced projects to enhance information systems and data projects to improve the nation's health. Based at CDC in Atlanta, GA.

The fellowship provides a two-year, competency-based training in public health informatics, consisting of 90% on-the-job training and 10% coursework in informatics, data science, and public health. Required activities include: working on public health informatics projects within the assigned host site; providing short-term technical assistance to federal, international, state, local, and territorial health departments and nonprofit agencies through special requests (Info-Aids); and designing, developing, implementing, enhancing, or evaluating an information system or artifact in the public health domain (capstone project). Fellows also attend a two-week orientation at the start of the program.

Day-to-day activities include: working with teams involved in research and development of public health information systems; conducting informatics evaluations on complex public health information systems; contributing to CDC's emergency response activities; and providing technical assistance to state and local health departments and international public health agencies through short-term assignments.

Qualifications: background in computer science, data analytics, data science, or a related field; interest in applying technical expertise to public health challenges. See the CDC PHIFP website for complete eligibility requirements.

Compensation and logistics: paid fellowship (stipend amount not stated; confirm via CDC PHIFP website). 2-year program. Based at CDC, Atlanta, GA. Application deadline: November 6, 2026.

item.company: Asian Pacific American Institute for Congressional Studies (APAICS)
item.title: Congressional Fellowship 2027-2028
item.description:
Application deadline: December 18, 2026 at 11:59 PM ET. A completed application must include: a cover letter expressing interest in the program; a one-page maximum resume; an academic transcript; two letters of recommendation (submitted by recommenders directly via the APAICS portal by December 18); and responses to three written questions (each no more than one page, double-spaced, 12-point Times New Roman font).

Note: APAICS Congressional Fellows are not employees of the federal government, their host office, or APAICS. Fellows receive a monthly educational stipend. Program dates: August 30, 2027–August 25, 2028. Washington, DC. This fellowship has a focus on Asian American, Native Hawaiian, and Pacific Islander (AAPI) communities and public policy.

The Asian Pacific American Institute for Congressional Studies (APAICS) Congressional Fellowship offers individuals the opportunity to serve our nation and deepen their understanding of public policy through participation in the legislative process. Fellows are placed with a congressional office or committee for 12 months and are given work equivalent to that of a congressional legislative aide. By the end of the fellowship, fellows will have established a professional network on Capitol Hill, understand how Congress operates, and acquired skills and expertise that make them marketable to congressional offices, federal agencies, nonprofits, and the private sector.

Each fellowship experience will differ depending on the office in which fellows are placed and the portfolio assigned; however, fellows gather as a cohort twice a month to discuss their experiences and for professional development opportunities. Fellows are also expected to attend APAICS-organized events including the Annual Awards Gala and policy summits, and must make a public presentation on a policy topic of their choosing toward the end of the fellowship year.

The three written questions ask applicants to: (1) describe how they envision the APAICS fellowship playing a role in their career path and what they hope to gain; (2) describe their experience in the U.S. with AAPI communities and how proximity to or distance from these communities has shaped their views on public policy; and (3) describe a time when they worked as part of a team and encountered a challenge.

Compensation and logistics: monthly educational stipend (amount not stated; confirm via APAICS). 12-month fellowship. Washington, DC. Program dates: August 30, 2027–August 25, 2028. Application deadline: December 18, 2026 at 11:59 PM ET.

item.title: Family Navigation Coordinator
item.description:
This position was posted with no close date and applications may be reviewed or closed on a rolling basis — interested applicants should apply ASAP! The posting will be removed from Batten Connect on 10/9/2026.

Note: This is a fixed-term position with an end date of September 30, 2027. This position is represented by the OPEIU union and is subject to the terms and conditions of a collective bargaining agreement. A valid driver’s license and access to a personal, insured vehicle are required. Bilingual skills (Spanish, Dari, Farsi, and/or Pashto) are desired. Charlottesville or Richmond, VA (hybrid). Salary 6.78–1.00/hr.

The International Rescue Committee (IRC) is one of the world’s largest international humanitarian NGOs, responding to the world’s worst humanitarian crises and helping to restore health, safety, education, economic wellbeing, and power to people devastated by conflict and disaster. The Family Navigation Coordinator will support IRC clients in building stability and eliminating identified barriers to allow clients to gain employment and achieve long-term self-sufficiency. The Coordinator works closely with colleagues across IRC programs and external partners to ensure clients have the knowledge and resources they need to thrive in their community. 2–3 years of relevant professional experience strongly preferred.

Key responsibilities include (Family Support): identifying and maintaining a resource list for clients including free or low-cost primary, specialty, dental, prescription, and mental healthcare options; providing tailored referral support for clients seeking healthcare resources within the community; coordinating initial health screenings; adapting and vetting culturally appropriate health education materials, communication, and educational workshops to build health system literacy and address health-related barriers to employment and self-sufficiency; coordinating initial school enrollment appointments and maintaining positive school relationships; collaborating with internal and external partners to make referrals and access services for early childhood applications, advocacy for services for children, parent engagement, educational workshops, and out-of-school time opportunities; and collaborating with internal and external partners to offer education and events for youth and families to thrive. (Partnership Building): maintaining and strengthening partnerships within established program priorities; attending partner meetings as directed by the casework supervisor and representing IRC within the scope of assigned tasks. (Documentation, Reporting, and Contract Compliance): coordinating data entry in compliance with IRC standards and grant requirements; and participating in staff meetings and training.

Qualifications: an undergraduate degree or equivalent experience; 2–3 years of relevant professional experience in human services, health navigation, education, youth programming, or nonprofit programs strongly preferred; experience with immigrant and refugee populations preferred; lived experience valued; knowledge of Virginia and/or U.S. public benefits, health, or school systems strongly preferred; strong relationship building, diplomacy, and networking skills; demonstrated success working in a multi-cultural environment; fluency in English (both spoken and written); proficiency in Spanish, Dari, Farsi, and/or Pashto desired; proficiency in Microsoft Office; valid driver’s license and access to a personal, insured vehicle required.

Compensation and logistics: salary 6.78–1.00/hr (~5,702–4,480 annualized). Comprehensive IRC benefits including medical starting at 63/month, dental starting at .50/month, vision starting at /month, 403(b) retirement savings with employer match, 10 sick days, 10 U.S. holidays, and 20–25 days of paid time off. Charlottesville or Richmond, VA (hybrid). OPEIU union position. Fixed-term through September 30, 2027. Driver’s license and personal insured vehicle required. Occasional weekend and/or evening work.

item.description:

Note: Entry-level position intended for candidates with 0-1 years of experience, available to start in Fall 2026. Hybrid in Arlington, VA or New York, NY (minimum 2 days in office). Salary $66,000 + $2,500 signing bonus.

ICF is a global advisory and technology services firm at the forefront of energy and climate consulting. The Energy and Climate Researcher will assist with research, data analysis, technical reviews, report writing, and engagement activities to support ICF's energy and climate planning consulting practice. Focus areas include energy and economic analyses, procurement and planning; regulatory and policy support; greenhouse gas accounting and management; infrastructure climate risk and resilience; and sustainability goal setting and performance management. The position has a particular focus on quantitative analyses and synthesizing research and data through statistical analyses, data visualization, and modeling.

Key responsibilities include: performing quantitative analyses and managing and analyzing large datasets; working with data analysis tools including Python, Microsoft Excel, R, and/or GIS for advanced statistical analysis, data visualization, and modeling; using Word, PowerPoint, Canva, and other tools to communicate and present information; using research and data to help tell a story and provide salient information for client decision-making; communicating complex technical and analytical information to both technical and non-technical audiences; and utilizing AI tools (e.g., CoPilot, ChatGPT) for research and task efficiencies.

Qualifications: a completed bachelor's degree by start date in Environmental Data Science, Oceanic and Atmospheric Sciences, Environmental or Energy Engineering, Economics, Chemistry, Math, Statistics, Environmental Sciences, Environmental Policy, Operations Research, or a similarly related field; demonstrated interest in energy, economic, climate, resilience, or sustainability topics; comfort performing quantitative analyses and managing large datasets; and strong writing skills. Experience with energy markets and economics, climate adaptation and resilience, sustainability practices/policies/regulations, programming, or client/community engagement is a plus.

Compensation and logistics: salary $66,000 + $2,500 signing bonus (0-1 years experience). Comprehensive ICF benefits. Arlington, VA or New York, NY (hybrid, minimum 2 days in office). Fall 2026 start. Entry-level.

The Robert J. Duke-Margolis is hiring multiple Policy Analysts to join the Institute's Biomedical Innovation research team, primarily supporting projects focused on the development, approval, and overall regulation of medical products, including engagement with the U.S. Food and Drug Administration. Volunteers live and work in host communities, receiving a stipend and other support including housing, medical care, and a readjustment allowance upon completion of service.

The Peace Corps is seeking U.S. citizens to serve as Youth Development Specialists in El Salvador. Youth make up more than a quarter of El Salvador's population, yet many young people face social and economic challenges including economic hardship, low school completion rates, limited life skills development opportunities, and barriers to civic engagement. Only half of youth complete lower secondary school and even fewer complete upper secondary school. As a Youth Development Specialist, you will collaborate with school staff to equip youth with essential life skills such as communication, empathy, creative problem-solving, and goal setting, working alongside community leaders to create supportive environments that encourage youth participation in community projects and civic engagement.

Key responsibilities include: collaborating with school staff to teach essential life skills to youth; working alongside community leaders to create supportive environments for youth participation; contributing to community projects and civic engagement initiatives; building relationships with host community members; and exchanging knowledge and helping transform lives for future generations.

Qualifications: U.S. citizenship required; bachelor's degree (typical requirement for Peace Corps service); demonstrated commitment to community development, education, or youth work. Visit the Peace Corps El Salvador project page for full details and application information.

Compensation and logistics: living stipend provided (not a salary); additional benefits include housing support, medical and dental care, language and cultural training, and a readjustment allowance upon completion of service. El Salvador. 2-year commitment. U.S. citizenship required.
